questions.q: What AWS service does Mara federate to Entra ID to build the consolidated identity view?
options: AWS Secrets Manager
AWS IAM Identity Center, using SAML 2.0 with Entra ID as the identity provider
Amazon Cognito
AWS Organizations' Service Control Policies
questions.explain: Mara enables AWS IAM Identity Center and configures SAML 2.0 federation with Entra ID as the identity provider, making Entra ID the single place authentication actually happens.

questions.q: Why is SCIM provisioning needed in addition to SAML federation?
options: SCIM is required purely for compliance paperwork, with no functional purpose
SAML federation alone only solves authentication; SCIM automatically syncs Entra ID group membership changes into IAM Identity Center so access stays current without a manual AWS-side step
SCIM replaces the need for any permission sets in AWS
SCIM is only needed for non-human workload identities
questions.explain: Federation solves sign-in; SCIM closes the sync gap by automatically provisioning or deprovisioning AWS access whenever Entra ID group membership changes, which is exactly the drift problem Lesson 3 found.

questions.q: How does the ScadaOTAdministrator permission set get assigned in the target design?
options: Directly to named individuals, one at a time
To the Entra ID group SCADA-OT-Admins, so anyone added to or removed from that group automatically gains or loses the AWS permission set via SCIM sync
It is assigned permanently and never re-evaluated
It is shared identically across all three Hartwell AWS accounts
questions.explain: Permission sets are assigned to the Entra ID group rather than individuals, so AWS access follows group membership automatically instead of requiring a second, manually maintained system.

questions.q: How does this consolidation directly address the long-lived access key finding from Lesson 3?
options: It doesn't — key rotation is a separate, unrelated project
Users identified with long-lived keys are migrated to federated, short-lived sessions through IAM Identity Center, and their standing IAM users and keys are then deactivated and deleted
It simply extends the expiration date on existing keys
It moves the long-lived keys to a more secure storage location without removing them
questions.explain: Migrating affected users to federated sessions and then deactivating their standing IAM users and access keys removes the long-lived credentials Lesson 3 flagged, rather than just documenting them.

questions.q: What is deliberately kept outside of this identity consolidation, and why?
options: Executive accounts, because they're considered too sensitive to federate

Non-human workload identities (like EC2 or Lambda service roles), because federation and SCIM solve human identity consolidation, and mixing in workload identity would recreate a different version of the same sprawl problem
The Hartwell-DevTest account, because it's being decommissioned
Nothing is kept outside — the plan consolidates every identity type into IAM Identity Center
questions.explain: Workload identities continue using AWS IAM roles directly, scoped per workload, because federation and SCIM are built for human identity — forcing non-human identity through the same model would create a new sprawl problem.
